No distinct circular spots, no powdery coating, no rust pustules. This suggests a viral disease or downy mildew. Top candidates: Bean_Pod_Mottle_virus, Soybean_Vein_necrosis_virus, Downy_mildew, Tobacco_Streak_Virus.

Let me view one reference from each candidate class first.
This Downy_mildew reference (Soybean_Dise_137) looks very similar to the test image — irregular yellowish-green blotches scattered across dark green leaves. Let me check more classes to compare.
Now let me cover the remaining required classes, one reference each.

I've now viewed 16 different classes. 

**Summary of analysis:**

- **Test image**: Multiple soybean leaves with irregular yellowish-green blotchy mottling scattered across the leaf surface, slightly puckered/wrinkled texture, no distinct circular spots, no necrosis.

- **Best match**: `Downy_mildew` (Soybean_Dise_137) — shows scattered irregular yellow-green blotches across dark green leaves with the same overall mottled appearance and leaf texture. Visually closest match.

- **Ruled out**: Bean_Pod_Mottle_virus (pod/seed symptoms), Soybean_Vein_necrosis_virus (necrotic vein lesions), Sudden_death_syndrome (severe interveinal necrosis), Septoria_brown_spot (discrete brown spots), Frogeye (circular spots), others showed stem/root/seed symptoms not matching leaf mottling.
